paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this passage. Twelve leaders walk the same land, taste the same fruit and see the same giants. Yet they don't all come back with the same answer. The LORD had already said the land was something He is giving to the Israelites (Numbers 13:2), and the spies had to decide what to do with that.

Look at how the report goes. They say the land is "flowing with milk and honey," and then comes the turn: "Nevertheless, the people living in the land are strong…" (Numbers 13:27-28). Caleb says, "We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!" (Numbers 13:30). The other men look at the same land and say, "We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!" (Numbers 13:31). I think the difference is what each group measured. One group counted the giants, and Caleb counted what the LORD had said.

So here's what I'd take home, baker. When you size yourself up next to a problem, you can end up with a grasshopper's view of the whole thing, and I know that feeling from my years in the back of a drawer. They said, "We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight," and then they guessed how they looked to the giants (Numbers 13:33). The question to carry with you is whether you're measuring by what you see or by what the LORD has said. And this story is NOT over, friend, so hold on to that question.
